results.input: A write made while the network is down is durably queued on the desk machine before the user is told anything, and survives a reload.
results.attackTest: tests/frontdesk/offline-contract.spec.ts:116 > the context is switched offline and the badge is flipped by a reachability probe rather than a guess, two writes are clicked, and BOTH rows are then read back out of the database the desk owns (indexedDB.open("silid-frontdesk") -> transaction("outbox") -> getAll()) in state "pending" — React state alone would pass this test and prove nothing — and after page.reload() both are still on screen; packages/offline-sync/test/outbox.test.ts > "is durable before the caller is told anything: a fresh connection sees the row" (a second Dexie connection opened after the write, i.e. the reload case). 12/12 offline-contract scenarios green 2026-09-26, on two independent full runs
results.evidence: EVIDENCE d2ac349 /Silid/packages/offline-sync/src/outbox.ts:92 — await db.outbox.add(entry): the row is committed to the desk's own IndexedDB before enqueue() resolves, so nothing is reported to the cashier that is not already on disk

results.input: When the network returns, queued writes replay in order, each exactly once, even if the connection drops again mid-drain.
results.attackTest: tests/frontdesk/offline-contract.spec.ts:158 > three writes queued offline, then reconnect: the run-scoped harness accept-log reads seq [1, 2, 3] and the outbox is empty; :281 > the connection drops AGAIN mid-drain (injected 503 on row 2) and the pass stops there — row 2 is back to pending with its attempt counted, row 3 is untouched, the ledger holds only [1], so nothing was lost and nothing was double-sent; :223 > the same envelope posted twice is answered from the first observation (coalesced: true, the original receivedAt) and the ledger still holds one row; packages/offline-sync/test/outbox.test.ts > "drains oldest-first, in the order the actions were taken", "coalesces a duplicate replay to one row via the idempotency key", "replays an entry that was in flight when the desk died, carrying the same key", "stops on a transport failure and leaves the rest pending for the next drain", "hands the transport the same key and the same instant it will queue under". 12/12 offline-contract scenarios green 2026-09-26, on two independent full runs
results.evidence: EVIDENCE d2ac349 /Silid/packages/offline-sync/src/outbox.ts:119 — drain(): oldest-first over listReplayable, one send per row under that row's own idempotency key, the row deleted only after the send resolves, and inflight rows replayed on purpose because the key — not the attempt count — is what settles a crash-after-send

results.input: A failed replay does not block the rest of the queue; the stuck entry is visible to the desk rather than silently lost.
results.attackTest: tests/frontdesk/offline-contract.spec.ts:249 > the fault is chosen when the write is QUEUED, because a replay carries the payload it was queued with — row 1 clean, row 2 injected-reject, row 3 clean: the drain reports "drained 2, poisoned 1, remaining 1", the ledger holds seq [1, 3], and the stuck row is on screen as "errored" carrying its 409 — visible, not lost; :281 > the other failure class (unreachable) stops the pass instead, because the next row would fail identically and each attempt would burn the desk's connectivity; packages/offline-sync/test/outbox.test.ts > "marks a rejected entry errored and keeps draining the rest", "keeps a rejection that is not an Error readable on the row", "never re-sends an errored entry", "counts each attempt so a repeatedly failing entry is visible". 12/12 offline-contract scenarios green 2026-09-26, on two independent full runs
results.evidence: EVIDENCE d2ac349 /Silid/packages/offline-sync/src/outbox.ts:148 — a server rejection marks the row errored with its reason and continues the pass; errored rows are then excluded from every later replay (outbox.ts:106) so the entry surfaces to a human instead of looping forever

results.input: The server stamps replayed writes with its own time; a client-supplied time is never stored as authoritative.
results.clip: reports/proof/e2e/frontdesk-offline-contract-2de72-tative-one-never-the-desk-s-frontdesk/video.webm (the companion strict-envelope scenario at :204 is a request-only test — it attacks the server boundary with no desk screen to record — so Playwright writes no clip for it)
results.attackTest: tests/frontdesk/offline-contract.spec.ts:184 > a write is queued offline, deliberately left to go stale for 1.1 s, then drained: the stored row's receivedAt is the server's accept instant and parses strictly later than the desk's enqueuedAt, and the desk's instant survives only as client metadata; :204 > a POST carrying a server-looking "receivedAt": "1999-01-01T00:00:00.000Z" is refused 400 harness_bad_envelope and the ledger records nothing; apps/frontdesk/test/harness-double.test.ts > "refuses an envelope carrying a server-looking timestamp field", "seals the accept instant with the server's own clock" (injected clock, so the seal is asserted, not observed); packages/offline-sync/test/outbox.test.ts > "records the local enqueue instant as metadata, never as an authoritative field", "sends the enqueue instant namespaced as client metadata, never as a server field". 12/12 offline-contract scenarios green 2026-09-26, on two independent full runs. The DoD's own pgTAP assertion is also RUN, not substituted: supabase/tests/13_replay_seal_test.sql, 18/18 green 2026-09-26 against the linked project through the Supabase MCP path. Five structural assertions read the catalog (no state-changing public function accepts a timestamp parameter, so a desk has no parameter to forge an instant into; authenticated holds no UPDATE or DELETE on any fact table; the only client-insertable tables without a BEFORE INSERT seal are exactly the four catalog tables, named rather than implied; every seal stamps clock_timestamp(); sessions.booked_end_at carries no column default so the overstay deadline is derived, not supplied). Nine behavioural assertions replay writes as a real cashier JWT carrying forged instants - 1999 on the ledgers, 2099 on the check-in that would move every overstay deadline - and forged actors, and read back that the stored value is the server's own clock. One more pins an asymmetry found while writing the suite: audit_log admits a cashier's INSERT but its SELECT policy admits only platform and org admins, so a client read-back returns nothing. The last three prove the second attack: a client cannot amend a stamped instant afterwards (42501, nothing written) and the refused amendment created nothing. Substitution disclosed: this host has no Docker daemon, so there is no local stack; the linked project is a real Postgres with real RLS, real grants and real triggers, and the suite is inside begin/rollback so it leaves no residue. The one property that is NOT proven, logged as a forward obligation in PROGRESS.md: no server-side idempotency store exists yet, so a duplicate replay cannot yet be coalesced by the database - the desk carries the key and the harness double coalesces on it, but no column anywhere in public is a dedupe key.
results.evidence: EVIDENCE d2ac349 /Silid/apps/frontdesk/src/lib/harness/double.ts:21 — the strict envelope: the only instant a desk may send is clientMetadata.enqueuedAt, and z.strictObject turns an accidental server-looking field into a rejection instead of a stored time; the row's own receivedAt is stamped from the server's clock (double.ts:78, 135). EVIDENCE a3415dc /Silid/supabase/tests/13_replay_seal_test.sql:1 — the same property asserted against a real Postgres: 18/18, five structural catalog assertions plus thirteen behavioural assertions driving five client writes under a real cashier JWT

results.input: Actions that must never run offline are visibly blocked while offline.
results.attackTest: tests/frontdesk/offline-contract.spec.ts:318 > offline, shift_close reports "BLOCKED (offline)" together with the reason the cashier is shown, void_session refuses the same way, and the identical click reports ALLOWED once the link is back — the gate is not simply stuck on; :342 > back ONLINE but with a money-affecting write still queued, shift_open still reports "BLOCKED (pending_money)" and only clears after the drain, proving the second block is the incomplete ledger rather than the link; packages/offline-sync/test/online-only.test.ts > all 8 cases, including "blocks every online-only action while offline" (all four: shift_open, shift_close, void_session, update_rate_config), "blocks a shift close while offline even with an empty outbox", "lets a void through when online even with queued money writes", and "rejects an action that is not in the online-only set". 12/12 offline-contract scenarios green 2026-09-26, on two independent full runs
results.evidence: EVIDENCE d2ac349 /Silid/packages/offline-sync/src/online-only.ts:36 — evaluateOnlineOnly(): the four sealed actions refuse with a NAMED reason (offline | pending_money) rather than a silent no-op, and the money-affecting queue count is consulted on the online path too, so a reachable server is not mistaken for a complete ledger

results.input: The Frontdesk installs as a PWA and its shell boots without a network connection.
results.attackTest: tests/frontdesk/offline-contract.spec.ts:67 > the served manifest.webmanifest declares display: standalone, start_url "/" and the generated icon set (a browser accepts it as installable), and the worker registered at /serwist/sw.js with scope "/" takes control of the desk; :95 > with the context switched offline AND the page reloaded, the entire shell renders from the worker's cache — heading, HARNESS-ONLY marker and queue note all visible with no server reachable at all; :370 > performance.timeOrigin is byte-identical across a reconnect, so the desk is not thrown back to a cold boot: SerwistProvider's default reloadOnOnline={true} attaches location.reload() to the window online event and would have wiped the live desk, which is the opposite of spec/offline-sync.md §5. 12/12 offline-contract scenarios green 2026-09-26, on two independent full runs
